subject: Onsite deployment license boundary and evidence — MSA / Order Form redline coordination
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@medsys-health.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajesh Patel <r.patel@medsys-health.com>
Date: Sun, 2 May 2027 14:15:00 -0700
Subject: Private/on-prem deployment — license footprint, operator access, evidence request

Hi Sergio,

Thanks for the demo earlier — Medsys is interested in the on‑prem deployment option for our clinical gateway. Before we proceed to a formal PO we need to align contract language and an evidence package so our InfoSec and Procurement teams can greenlight the deployment. High level asks: 

- Confirm license boundary: we need explicit language that the license covers the Redwood runtime + model weights you ship, and that we are not licensing model training IP. Please propose precise MSA/Order Form language.
- Operator access: we require operator access controls and a written attestation describing who can access logs, snapshots, and operator consoles.
- Audit & escrow-like options: we have a regulatory requirement to be able to obtain an 'execution snapshot' and evidence of access in a continuity event. We don't need source code escrow today, but would like options for custody/escrow of keys or snapshots and a process for third‑party attestation.
- Evidence matrix: SOC 2 scope, retention windows for logs, and how operator actions are logged.

Can you share suggested redlines for the MSA and Order Form and an evidence matrix that InfoSec can review? Ideally by EOD Wednesday so our procurement cycle keeps momentum.

Thanks,
Elena Morales
Head of IT Security, Medsys Health
elena.morales@medsys-health.com

Attachments: (none in this message)
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@medsys-health.com>
Cc: Rajesh Patel <r.patel@medsys-health.com>, laura.bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, hiro.tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private/on-prem deployment — license footprint, operator access, evidence request

Elena — thank you, and great to hear Medsys is moving forward. I attached an initial set of redlines for the MSA and a marked Order Form plus an evidence matrix that maps the items your InfoSec team asked for to the artifacts we can provide. Quick summary of our proposals: 

- License boundary: proposed clause narrows the license to the runtime, shipped model binaries (specific model versions enumerated in the Order Form), and excludes training data/weights and model development IP. We add a schedule that lists permitted internal uses (serving in production, internal testing for integration).
- Operator access: proposed operator ACLs (role/identity based) and an attestation template we can sign monthly. Operator actions (console logins, snapshot export, operator-initiated restores) are logged and retained per the evidence matrix.
- Audit/escrow-lite: we included two paths in the Order Form: (A) monthly signed snapshot transfer plus hash evidence (we retain custody of encrypted snapshots and provide a notarized hash on request) or (B) third‑party attestation protocol where an auditor can verify snapshot integrity at a scheduled window. This is not full source escrow but should meet your continuity requirement.

Timeline: Laura (legal) and Hiro (ops) are looped to tighten language. I can deliver updated redlines after legal review by EOD Tuesday. If InfoSec needs a demo of the snapshot process, we can schedule a 30m call this week.

Next steps: 1) Laura to review redlines, 2) Hiro to confirm log retention and snapshot export mechanics, 3) I will share refined documents and a proposed DocuSign flow.

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Attachments: suggested_redline_MSA.docx; orderform_redline.pdf; evidence_matrix.xlsx
From: laura.bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>, hiro.tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private/on-prem deployment — license footprint, operator access, evidence request

Sergio / Hiro,

I reviewed the suggested_redline_MSA.docx and have the following legal comments (high level):

1) License scope — good start. We should explicitly state: (a) "Model binaries" are the deliverable and include a version identifier; (b) "Model improvements" language must be excluded unless both parties sign a separate addendum.
2) Limits on reverse engineering — add carve-outs for debugging by Customer security teams under a mutual NDA and with redaction obligations.
3) Audit and escrow-lite — the two-path approach is sensible. However, procurement may push for a defined trigger for snapshot release (e.g., insolvency, failure to meet SLA for >30 days). We can accept 'continuity event' language but must narrow for legal clarity and include notice/cure windows.
4) Operator access attestation — legal wants a concrete format (we should attach an attestation template) and retention period not to exceed 18 months unless agreed.

I attached inline comments in the docx. Hiro, please confirm the practical mechanics for: encrypted snapshot retention, key custody options (customer‑managed KMS vs Redwood HSM), and typical timelines to produce an auditor's package.

If Procurement wants an evidence transfer as a condition of signing, we must confirm timelines — I don't recommend holding execution on an initial PO pending full third‑party audit; propose phased milestones instead.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

Attachments: (inline comments in suggested_redline_MSA.docx)

Hiro's brief confirmation: snapshot exports are encrypted with customer‑managed KMS as an option; default is Redwood-managed encryption with HSM-backed keys. We can produce a notarized hash within 5 business days and a full auditor package (logs + hash validation) within 15 business days. Export process requires coordination with our SRE on a scheduled maintenance window.

From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@medsys-health.com>

Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private/on-prem deployment — license footprint, operator access, evidence request

Sergio — thanks for the quick turnaround and for looping legal/ops. The updated artifacts look promising. A few quick items from InfoSec / Procurement: 

- The two-path escrow-lite option is acceptable; Procurement will still want the continuity trigger defined (we prefer insolvency or Redwood ceasing to provide the service for >30 days). Please align language to that narrow trigger and include a notice/cure period.
- We prefer the customer‑managed KMS option. Can you add explicit steps in the evidence matrix for key handover or key‑unwrap proof?
- Can you confirm retention windows in evidence_matrix_v2.xlsx (logs: 12 months, snapshots: 24 months)? If legal insists on 18 months for attestation retention, we need a clear exception for snapshots used for regulatory continuity.

I'll confirm the 30m call after I check with Rajesh. If Procurement can get your final redlines by Thursday EOD, we can target a PO the following week.

Thanks,
Elena
